Figure 2:One score versus checkable evidenceon the same recording, in which one word of genuine speech was
replaced by synthesized speech. Asked directly, the model judges the recording genuine (left). Asked to reason,VeriSpoof-Basestates observations, a synthesized span and a source profile before deciding (right). Each statement is
checked against a waveform measurement or a label (✓\checkmarkholds,×\timesfails, – no label), and replacing the
stated span by “none” flips the decision. Statements are abridged; the full output is in
Figure11.

Figure 3:VeriSpoof.(1) An 8 s waveform, or two for a pair, enters (2) the Qwen3-ASR
encoder, frozen apart from DoRA adapters. (3) Two learned mixes over its 25 layers feed (4) the audio tokenizer, which pools the recording into 16 utterance
tokens and stacks pairs of frames with a text time marker every 0.8 s. (5) The prompt
places the tokens of A, then those of B, before the question; (6) the frozen LLM with LoRA reads it and (7) returns a
score, the log-likelihood difference of two answer sentences, a rationale whose decision comes last, or a per-token
synthetic-speech profile. Grey: frozen; dark blue: trained by us, with the stages that train each part (PA: perception
alignment, QT: forensic question tuning, RT: grounded rationale tuning).
